analysis.headline: A Met Office amber wind warning covers Edinburgh from 9 pm tonight (Saturday) to 9 pm Sunday, with severe west-south-westerly gales after heavy evening rain. Another gale is likely on Tuesday, then high pressure brings a quieter, drier spell from Thursday.
analysis.summary: Two official warnings are in force for Lothian Borders. A yellow wind warning runs from 12:00 BST today to 21:00 GMT Sunday, and an amber wind warning from 21:00 BST tonight to 21:00 GMT Sunday. The clocks go back at 02:00 BST Sunday. A very deep low, about 949-953 hPa in ECMWF, ICON, ARPEGE, AIFS and GEM, passes close to the north of Scotland overnight. It brings 8-15 mm of rain this evening, then severe gales: model gusts at Edinburgh are 93-127 km/h on Sunday, with UKMO at 96 and ARPEGE the highest at 127. Monday turns briefly mild, with 850 hPa temperatures near +10 °C, highs of about 15 °C and rain later in the day. A second windy spell with a cold front follows on Tuesday, with gusts of 84-109 km/h across the models. Pressure then rises: a high builds over the UK on Thursday 29th and over the North Sea and Scandinavia into early November, giving mostly dry, calmer weather with near-normal temperatures and some fog or frost risk later. There is no low-level snow risk: 850 hPa temperatures bottom out around -1 to -3 °C, well short of the -5 °C threshold.

days.summary: Rather cloudy and breezy, with rain arriving this afternoon and turning heavy this evening (about 8-15 mm, mostly 18:00-24:00). Southerly winds back south-westerly and rise sharply tonight as the amber warning begins at 21:00 BST.
days.wind: S to SW, strengthening; gusts 75-100 km/h by late evening (amber warning from 21:00 BST)

days.summary: Clocks go back. Severe W-SW gales overnight and through Sunday (amber warning until 21:00 GMT), with bands of blustery showers or rain, wettest early. It feels raw despite mild air at first; turning colder aloft in the evening, and only the highest Scottish hills might see sleet. Winds ease after dark.
days.wind: W-SW severe gale; gusts 90-110 km/h widely, locally higher on exposed ground and bridges (models 93-127 km/h)

days.summary: A brighter, quieter start, then cloud thickens and rain spreads in from the south-west in the afternoon and evening (about 3-8 mm). Much milder air arrives on a strengthening southerly.
days.wind: S to SW, fresh to strong; gusts 60-75 km/h, higher later

days.summary: Mild, windy and often cloudy in the warm sector. A cold front brings a spell of rain and a wind shift later. Rain totals vary between models (about 1-9 mm). A second gale is likely.
days.wind: SW gale; gusts 85-105 km/h (ICON, GEM and ARPEGE about 105-109 km/h; ECMWF 84 km/h); no warning yet

days.summary: Fresher behind the front, with sunny spells and a few showers, mostly light (0-3 mm). Winds slowly ease.
days.wind: W to NW, fresh; gusts 50-75 km/h, easing

days.summary: High pressure builds over the UK. Dry, with variable cloud and light winds; a mild night.
days.wind: Light to moderate W-SW; gusts 30-45 km/h

days.summary: Mostly dry under high pressure, but a weakening front may brush through with patchy light rain (about half of ensemble members have more than 1 mm). Otherwise cloudy and mild.
days.wind: Light to moderate S to SE; gusts 25-40 km/h

medium_range.summary: Days 7-16 (31 Oct to about 9 Nov): ensembles agree strongly on a blocked pattern early in the period. ECMWF HRES has the high over the North Sea at about 1027-1032 hPa on Saturday 31st, and west to north-west of Scotland at 1030-1034 hPa by 3 Nov. The ECMWF ENS mean centres a 1030 hPa high over the North Sea and Scandinavia at day 10. The AIFS ENS mean has 1030 hPa over Scandinavia and the Baltic, with only 4-8 hPa spread over the UK. JMA (1035-1040 hPa over Germany and Poland), AIFS and GEM are similar. The GEFS mean is less blocked, keeping the Atlantic trough closer to Ireland and the UK on the edge of the high. For Edinburgh that means mostly dry weather (ensemble means 0.1-0.5 mm per 6 h), light winds and temperatures near normal: daytime about 9-11 °C, nights 3-6 °C, colder in clear spells. Ensemble mean 850 hPa temperatures sit around +1 to +3 °C, close to climatology, but the cold tail widens. ECMWF p10 falls to about -3 °C by 6-8 Nov, GEFS p10 to about -6 °C by 9 Nov and GEM ENS p10 to about -4 °C, a sign that some members drift a cooler continental or north-easterly flow towards Scotland. Ground frost and fog become possible. ECMWF ENS gives 2-4% of members an air frost on 4-5 Nov, with the lowest member at -1.4 °C. By day 15 the AIFS ENS spread rises to 12-18 hPa over the UK and North Atlantic, and the AIFS deterministic run brings a deep Atlantic trough west of Ireland with the UK in a southerly flow. Whether and when the block gives way is therefore low confidence beyond about 5 Nov.
signals: Strong agreement on high pressure over or near the UK from 29 Oct to about 5 Nov: dry, light winds, fog and frost risk rather than rain.
No meaningful low-level snow signal: 850 hPa ensemble means stay at +1 to +3 °C. Only the colder 10% of members dip to -3 to -6 °C after 6 Nov.
ECMWF ENS frost probability is small (2-4% of members on 4-5 Nov); ensemble daily minimums mostly 3-6 °C.
Rainfall well below normal for the first week of November (ECMWF extended range: weekly rainfall anomaly negative, MSLP +10 to +20 hPa over the UK and North Sea).
Spread grows quickly after about 6 Nov (AIFS ENS MSLP spread 12-18 hPa by 8 Nov); the Atlantic may return around 8-12 Nov.

model_agreement.summary: Agreement is excellent through Sunday on the deep low and severe gales; the official amber warning and every model support it. Models differ on Sunday rain totals: AIFS has 23 mm and its ensemble about 18 mm, against about 2-11 mm in the physics models. AIFS has also over-forecast rain at this point recently (14 mm forecast against 3.7 mm observed on 15 Oct), so it is down-weighted for rain. Tuesday's gale is in all models, but its strength varies (gusts 84-109 km/h), as does the frontal rain (0.5-8 mm). On the verification scorecard, ICON and UKMO have the lowest temperature errors at short range. ECMWF HRES has a persistent cold bias on daytime highs (about -1.3 °C), so its highs are nudged up about 1 °C. Beyond day 5 the ensembles are preferred, and they agree on a blocking high from 29 Oct. The GEFS mean is a little more mobile than the ECMWF and AIFS ensembles.

models.view: Low about 950 hPa near the Faroes Sunday 02:00, with very tight gradients over Scotland. Gusts 93 km/h Sunday and 84 km/h Tuesday. Builds a high over the North Sea by 31 Oct and NW of Scotland about 1030-1034 hPa by 3 Nov. Cold bias on highs of about 1.3 °C in recent verification.

Tight clustering to day 5: rain 14.6 mm Saturday and 7.6 mm Sunday, 850 hPa spike to about +10 °C Monday evening. After 31 Oct spread widens (850 hPa p10-p90 about -3 to +7 °C) around a near-climate mean, with low rain. The EPSgram shows maximums near or slightly below model climate in early November.

Same synoptic pattern as the physics models: low about 952 hPa near Shetland, then the high. Much wetter for Sunday (23 mm; ensemble mean 18.5 mm), an outlier. A little milder than ECMWF in early November (AIFS ENS mean 850 hPa about +3 °C). The control and deterministic runs are on the warm side of their ensemble. Best day-1 temperature error but weaker wet/dry skill at days 5-7 (60-63%).

Gusts 96 km/h Sunday and 87 km/h Tuesday; highs about 16 °C Monday and Tuesday; drier than ECMWF on Tuesday and Wednesday. Its ensemble keeps Wednesday mostly dry (11% chance of more than 1 mm). Among the best recent temperature scores.

Windier: gusts 100 km/h Saturday and 105 km/h Sunday, then 91 km/h Tuesday and 87 km/h Wednesday. The GEFS mean keeps an Atlantic trough nearer the UK at days 10-15, giving a less robust block. The GEFS plume has the coldest tail (p10 near -6 °C at 850 hPa by 9 Nov). Good recent wet/dry hit rate (77-83%).
Low about 952 hPa; gusts 94 km/h Sunday and the joint-strongest Tuesday gusts (109 km/h). Mild Monday and Tuesday (about 16 °C). Lowest temperature error at days 1-3 in the scorecard.
Very windy: gusts 106-111 km/h Saturday-Sunday, 109 km/h Tuesday. Builds a strong ridge by 29-31 Oct. Its ensemble is a little milder, with a wide p10-p90 spread into November.
Deepest low (about 949 hPa) and the strongest Sunday gust at Edinburgh (127 km/h), plus 106 km/h on Tuesday. Supports the top end of the amber warning.
Both show the deep low NW of Scotland on Tuesday (about 955 hPa), then a strong continental high (JMA 1035-1040 hPa over central Europe and Scandinavia by 3 Nov). This confirms the blocking signal.

extended_range.summary: The ECMWF extended range (23 Oct run) has a short, strongly NAO-positive stormy spell now. A pronounced blocking episode follows from about 29 Oct to 8 Nov, with weekly MSLP anomalies of +10 to +20 hPa centred over the UK and North Sea. The extended meteogram for Edinburgh gives weekly temperature anomalies close to zero throughout: about +1 °C for the week to 2 Nov, then 0 to +0.5 °C each week to early December, and generally inside the model-climate range. Rainfall is below normal in the first two weeks of November, then near or slightly above normal from late November. The MSLP anomaly fades from strongly positive in early November to slightly negative by early December, indicating a gradual return to Atlantic westerlies. The weekly 2 m temperature maps put the coldest anomalies over central and eastern Europe under the block (2-9 Nov), with the UK near normal. The UK then turns slightly mild (0 to +1 °C) from mid-November into early December.

weeks.pattern: Stormy NAO-positive start (gales 25 and 27 Oct), then a high building over the UK from 29 Oct
Blocking high over the UK, North Sea and Scandinavia (MSLP +10 to +20 hPa); dry, light winds, fog and frost risk; cold air stays mainly over the continent
Block weakening; mixed regimes (blocking about 30-35%, NAO+ about 20%, Atlantic Ridge 15-25%); a slow return of Atlantic fronts
Near-normal pressure over the UK, slightly low in the mid-Atlantic; changeable with no strong signal
NAO+ share rising (30-40%); westerlies more likely, slightly mild
Weak low-pressure anomaly west of and over the UK; Atlantic, unsettled and slightly mild

extended_range.regimes: NAO+ has 100% probability on 24-26 Oct, matching the current storm, and 70-75% on 27-28 Oct. Blocking then dominates at 70-94% from 29 Oct to about 4 Nov, still 50-60% to about 8 Nov. Through mid-November the mix is roughly 30-35% blocking, about 20% NAO+, 15-25% Atlantic Ridge and 5-15% NAO-. By late November and early December NAO+ climbs to 30-40%, with blocking about 25-30% and NAO- 10-15%. For Edinburgh this means a dry, settled early November (frost and fog rather than snow, since the block's cold air sits over the continent), then increasingly westerly, mild and wetter weather towards December. NAO- and Atlantic Ridge, the regimes that bring northerly or easterly cold to Scotland, never exceed about 15-25%.
extended_range.polar_vortex: The 10 hPa zonal-mean wind falls sharply from about 22 m/s now to an ensemble mean near 11 m/s around 6 Nov, against a climatology of about 25 m/s. That is a notably weak early-season vortex, consistent with the tropospheric blocking. Only a handful of members (under about 5%) briefly reverse to slightly easterly winds (around 5-6 Nov, 13 Nov, 20 Nov and 27 Nov), so there is no meaningful sudden-warming signal. The mean then recovers strongly to about 37 m/s by 7 Dec, above the roughly 31 m/s climatology, which favours a westerly, NAO-positive early winter rather than a stratosphere-driven cold spell.

winter_outlook.summary: The guidance still tilts towards a mild and somewhat wet first half of winter, with a weaker, uncertain lean towards colder, blockier spells in late winter, mainly February. UK seasonal skill is modest, so treat these as nudges to the odds. SEAS5 tercile maps put Scotland mostly in the upper temperature tercile: about 60-100% for NDJ, 60-100% for DJF, 50-70% for JFM and 70-100% for FMA. C3S multi-model, SEAS5 and GloSea DJF anomalies are about +0.5 to +1 °C for Scotland. SEAS5 DJF rainfall leans wet (50-60% upper tercile), with lower pressure over the Atlantic and UK beneath higher pressure over Greenland and Iceland. That is an NAO-negative-looking pattern, but its southward-displaced storm track keeps Scotland cyclonic and wet rather than cold and easterly. At the Edinburgh grid point (raw, not bias-corrected), 80% of SEAS5 members are milder than normal in November and 65% in December, but only 55% in January and 35% in February. February also has about 11 frost days against a normal of 8.3, and the SEAS5 NAO median falls to about -1.6 in January and -2.5 in February. A very strong El Niño and a vortex expected to recover to above-normal strength by early December make a cold winter overall unlikely. A colder late-winter spell with some snow remains plausible.

months.notes: SEAS5 point: 7.1 °C against a 6.3 °C normal, 80% of members milder, 68 mm against 73 mm, 2 frost days against 3.3. C3S +0.5 to +1 °C and slightly wet regionally. The ECMWF extended range has a dry, blocked first week (frost and fog rather than snow), then a gradual Atlantic return.

SEAS5: 4.8 °C against 4.1 °C, 65% milder, 85 mm against 77 mm, 6 frost days against 8.3. NAO median about 0 with wide spread. The vortex is forecast above normal strength by early December, and the extended range shows slightly mild, westerly weather at the start of December.
SEAS5: 3.6 °C against 3.9 °C, 55% milder, 73 mm against 74 mm, 10 frost days against 8.2. NAO median about -1.6, while C3S still leans slightly mild (+0.5 to +1 °C).

The strongest cold tilt at the point: 3.4 °C against 4.1 °C, only 35% milder, 11 frost days against 8.3, NAO median about -2.5. C3S is near neutral to slightly mild for Scotland, so this is a weak tilt only.
SEAS5: 4.8 °C against 5.3 °C, 41% milder, 9 frost days against 5.7, 65 mm against 60 mm, NAO about -0.8. By contrast, the JFM and FMA tercile maps lean mild (50-100% upper tercile).

drivers: Very strong El Niño: the SEAS5 Niño 3.4 plume rises from about +3.6 °C in October to about +4.1-4.3 °C in December, and is still +2.4 to +3.8 °C in April. This tends to favour an active Atlantic jet early, with an NAO-negative tendency in late winter.
SEAS5 NAO medians by month: October about +2, November about -0.4, December about 0, January about -1.6, February about -2.5, March about -0.8, all with very wide spread.
SEAS5 DJF MSLP: +2 to +4 hPa over Greenland and Iceland, -2 to -4 hPa over the central Atlantic, -1 to -2 hPa over the UK. This is a cyclonic, wet setup for Scotland rather than a cold easterly one.
C3S 500 hPa heights: strong positive anomaly over Labrador and SW Greenland (+4 to +8 dam in DJF and JFM), near zero over the UK, positive over the Mediterranean.

Stratospheric vortex: weak in early November (mean about 11 m/s against about 25 m/s climatology) with no robust reversal, then recovering to above normal (about 37 m/s) by early December. This supports the November block but works against an early-winter cold regime.
Warm background climate and warm surrounding seas: SEAS5, C3S and GloSea all show the UK in the upper tercile or +0.5 to +1 °C across the season.
Cool SST and temperature anomaly south of Greenland in the C3S and SEAS5 maps, consistent with an active Atlantic storm track.

hazards.when: 21:00 BST Sat 24 Oct to 21:00 GMT Sun 25 Oct
hazards.what: Met Office AMBER wind warning (severe, likely) for Lothian Borders: severe W-SW gales with gusts of about 90-110 km/h, locally higher on exposed ground. Expect disruption to travel (bridges, rail, ferries), possible power cuts, falling trees and flying debris.

hazards.when: 12:00 BST Sat 24 Oct to 21:00 GMT Sun 25 Oct
hazards.what: Met Office YELLOW wind warning covering the wider period around the amber warning.
Heavy rain ahead of the gales (about 8-15 mm in 6 hours), with blocked drains and leaf-clogged gutters giving surface water on roads.
A second gale with the cold front: gusts of about 85-105 km/h in most models. Not yet covered by a warning, so check for updates.
Fog and patchy frost on clear, calm nights under high pressure.

analysis.changes_since_last: The Friday yellow rain warning has expired. The yellow and amber wind warnings are unchanged in timing, and the amber area still covers Lothian Borders. Sunday's peak gust guidance has edged up: the model range is now 93-127 km/h, with ARPEGE highest, against 77-114 km/h before. The low is about 949-953 hPa rather than 945. Saturday evening's rain is now the main rain event (about 8-15 mm) rather than Friday's. Tuesday's gale is still expected, and ICON and GEM are stronger at about 109 km/h. The incoming high now looks a little less intense near the UK: ECMWF has 1027-1034 hPa, with the 1035-1040 hPa centres placed over Scandinavia and central Europe rather than over Scotland. ECMWF's 850 hPa p10 drops to about -3 °C by 6-8 Nov, so the cold tail is slightly wider. On the seasonal side, the SEAS5 November point forecast is now milder and drier (7.1 °C, 80% of members milder, 68 mm, against 6.6 °C, 65% and 81 mm before), and December is 65% milder against 69%. Otherwise the winter outlook is unchanged.

chart_notes.note: ECMWF HRES, Sunday 02:00: low about 950 hPa near the Faroes with very tight isobars over Scotland, the setup behind the amber wind warning.
ECMWF HRES, Tuesday 02:00: new deep low about 959 hPa SW of Iceland, with a strong SSW flow and the mild warm sector over Scotland ahead of Tuesday's gale and cold front.
ECMWF HRES, Saturday 31 Oct: high about 1027-1032 hPa over the North Sea and Scandinavia covering the UK, giving dry, calm weather.
ECMWF ENS mean, 3 Nov: 1030 hPa high over the North Sea and Scandinavia, with the Atlantic trough held west. Strong ensemble support for blocking.
GEFS mean, 3 Nov: less blocked than ECMWF, with the Atlantic trough nearer Ireland and the UK on the western edge of the European high.
AIFS ENS, 8 Nov: MSLP spread 12-18 hPa over the North Atlantic, UK and Scandinavia, so the breakdown timing is low confidence.
ECMWF ENS plume: tight agreement on the 850 hPa spike to +10 °C on Monday evening and the rain peaks on Saturday evening and Monday evening, then a dry spell.
ECMWF EPSgram: very strong wind on Sunday and Tuesday. Daily highs about 10-14 °C this week, then near or slightly below model climate (about 10-11 °C) in early November, with low daily rainfall.
Weather regimes: NAO+ at 100% now, switching to blocking at 70-94% from 29 Oct to about 4 Nov, then a mixed regime and a rising NAO+ share by late November.
Weekly MSLP anomaly for 2-9 Nov: +10 to +20 hPa centred over the UK, North Sea and southern Scandinavia, a classic blocked, dry week.
10 hPa zonal wind: the vortex weakens to a mean of about 11 m/s by 6 Nov, with only a few members briefly reversing, then recovers above normal (about 37 m/s) by early December.
SEAS5 DJF temperature: the UK is mainly in the 60-100% upper-tercile category, a clear mild tilt.
SEAS5 DJF MSLP: high over Greenland and Iceland and low over the Atlantic and UK, which looks NAO-negative but is cyclonic and wet for Scotland.
SEAS5 NAO: the median turns negative in January (about -1.6) and February (about -2.5), the main hint of colder late-winter spells.
Niño 3.4 plume: a very strong El Niño peaking around +4 °C or more in December.
